clue.text: Riser bored mistakenly into old sewers

definitions.note: plural noun, matching the plural answer

indicators.note: done mistakenly, the letters of riser bored are put together the wrong way and must be reordered

explanation.surface: A rising damp or a boring tool has wrongly broken into an ancient drainage system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewers' looks like drains, but here it means people who sew; 'into' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Broiderers is an archaic word for embroiderers, people who stitch decorative needlework.

clue.text: It increases potency by way of agar regularly added to start with

parts.note: via means by way of

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of agar, the second and fourth

parts.note: the even letters of agar

indicators.note: to start with points at the opening letter of added

parts.note: first letter of added

explanation.surface: A lab note: potency rises when a culture medium is routed through and topped up with agar.
explanation.definitionFit: The brand-name drug is taken to treat erectile dysfunction, boosting male sexual potency.

clue.text: People dance here exclusively

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... Come Dancing, the BBC ballroom-dancing TV show, known as ...

explanation.walkthrough: Strictly Come Dancing is a popular British TV contest in which celebrities partner professional dancers; everyone calls it Strictly.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means only or solely, and it is also the short title of the BBC dance show.

clue.text: Sheathing of icebreaker incorporates a certain compound

indicators.note: incorporates means takes something into its body, so one piece goes inside the other
the sheathing of a word is its outer covering, its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of icebreaker
some means a certain, as in some person or other

explanation.surface: The hull covering of an icebreaker ship contains a particular chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: An isomer is a chemical compound sharing its molecular formula with another but differing in structure.

clue.text: White van caught carrying illicit blini not the last

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so the van holds the next piece
illicit means unlawful, bent, so the letters are bent into a new order
not the last means the final letter of blini is dropped

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A white van is stopped by police and found to be smuggling contraband Russian pancakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White van' looks like a vehicle, but 'White' alone is the definition; blini are small Russian pancakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Vin blanc is French for white wine, so 'White' is the wine in shorthand, as in a glass of white.

clue.text: Sounds like puncture for flier

indicators.note: sounds like says the answer is spoken the same as a word for the next clue word

parts.note: to skewer is to pierce or puncture

explanation.surface: A bird's cry resembles the sound of a tyre getting a puncture.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent skewer and the seabird's name are said alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The skua is a large predatory seabird, and any bird is a flier.

clue.text: Soccer's "Fifth official", say, brand-new — and he's troublesome

parts.note: VAR, the video assistant referee, is in effect a further official in a football match
mint means brand-new, as in mint condition

explanation.surface: A newly appointed extra match official proves a nuisance on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: VAR is the video assistant referee used in football (soccer) to review decisions.
explanation.definitionFit: A varmint is a dialect word for a mischievous, troublesome person or animal, a pest.

clue.text: Plum's over misfortune, gaining ultimate recognition

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a Victoria is a variety of plum; the 's is short for is
a cross is a trouble or misfortune, as in a cross to bear

explanation.surface: A man called Plum is over a stroke of bad luck and earning the highest praise.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victoria Cross is Britain's highest military award for gallantry, the ultimate honour.

clue.text: Robbery from post?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to ... a notice is to post it

explanation.walkthrough: 'from' just links the two senses; the second is the phrasal verb stick up, as with a poster.
explanation.definitionFit: A hold-up at gunpoint is a stick-up, and putting a notice up on a board is posting it.

clue.text: Foretell crazy operating cost

indicators.note: crazy means mad, so the letters of operating cost go haywire into a new order

explanation.surface: A wild guess at what the running costs of a business will be.
explanation.definitionFit: To prognosticate is to predict or prophesy future events.

clue.text: Essentially, director's movie featuring Heather is a wrap

indicators.note: featuring means having as a part, so the heather goes inside
essentially points at the essence, the central letter of director's

parts.note: the middle letter of director's
film means movie
ling is the common heather plant

explanation.surface: A film director finishes a picture starring an actress called Heather: 'It's a wrap!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a star's name but is the plant. 'It's a wrap' is film slang for finished shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: Clingfilm is thin plastic sheeting used to wrap food, so it is literally a wrap.

clue.text: Somewhat misdescribe anodyne celebration

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone rather plays down a party by calling it bland.
explanation.definitionFit: A beano is British slang for a lively party or knees-up.

clue.text: Termination of painful menage a trois — nastier characters departing

indicators.note: painful suggests something tortured, so the letters are twisted into a new order
the characters of nastier leave the mix, so they are taken out of the fodder

explanation.surface: A messy love triangle ends badly once the nastiest people walk out.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters N,A,S,T,I,E,R out of MENAGEATROIS and M,E,G,A,O remain to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, hence the end or termination of anything.

clue.text: Girl briefly sat next to Jack for protection

indicators.note: sat next to means the two pieces are placed side by side

parts.note: jack and tar are both slang for a sailor

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter of the name goes

parts.note: Pauline is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman sits beside a man named Jack, who looks after her.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin is a heavy waterproof sheet used as a covering to shelter things from rain.

clue.text: Sweeps last of junk up in mad hurry

indicators.note: in means the reversed piece is placed inside the word for mad

parts.note: loopy is informal for mad

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pieces read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a camera pans when it sweeps across a scene

indicators.note: last of points at the final letter of junk

parts.note: last letter of junk

explanation.surface: Someone frantically clears away the last of the rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweeps' looks like cleaning, but it is a camera's sweeping movement; the reversed block splits the word for mad after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Look snappy is an idiom urging someone to be quick, to get a move on.

clue.text: If possible, put notion to partner with only one answer called for

indicators.note: with only one says that of the two answer letters in the pieces, one is dropped
called for means only one is needed, so the spare letter is removed

parts.note: an idea is a notion
an ally is a partner

explanation.surface: Advice: where you can, share your idea with a colleague, needing only a single reply.
explanation.walkthrough: The two pieces meet with a doubled answer letter where they join, and 'only one answer called for' asks for that double to be reduced to a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideally means in the best case, as one would wish, given the chance.

clue.text: Get ahead having bound part of the hoof

parts.note: a bound is a leap
the frog is the V-shaped pad of horn on the underside of a horse's hoof

explanation.surface: A horse surges forward with a jump of its hooves.
explanation.definitionFit: To leapfrog is to jump ahead of others, overtaking them in rank or progress.

clue.text: Universities host band in holidays, being unoccupied

indicators.note: in means the university letters go inside the word for holidays

parts.note: vacs is informal for vacations, holidays

indicators.note: to host is to have something within, so the band goes between the two U's

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university, twice for the plural
a ring-shaped band looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Campuses put on a music group during the vacation, when no students are there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks like a music group, but it is the ring shape O.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacuous means empty or vacant, containing nothing.

clue.text: Atmosphere almost rendered cold with Disney's latest animation

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for atmosphere is left off

parts.note: a vibe is a mood or atmosphere
to render a tune is to run through it; ran means rendered
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: latest points at the final letter of Disney

parts.note: last letter of Disney

explanation.surface: A chilly feeling in a cartoon, as Disney's newest animated film is screened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'animation' looks like cartoons, a Disney theme, but it means liveliness.
explanation.definitionFit: Animation in the sense of liveliness and energy is a synonym for vibrancy.

clue.text: Device placed on Spanish shore was very steep

indicators.note: the device is placed on, after, the shore

parts.note: costa is Spanish for coast or shore
a bomb is an explosive device

explanation.surface: An explosive is left on a Spanish beach that dropped away sharply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steep' here is about price, not slope.
explanation.definitionFit: To cost a bomb is a British idiom for being very expensive, steep in price.

clue.text: Twist vivid gold as container

indicators.note: as container means the gold letters hold the other piece inside

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
live, as in a live wire, means vivid or vibrant

explanation.surface: A bright gold vessel is turned around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twist' looks like a verb, but it is a surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Twist is Dickens's orphan hero, so the first name pairs with the surname Twist.

clue.text: Get lost among diggers, perhaps, with setter's upper garments half destroyed

parts.note: the setter is, said by the setter, is I'm

indicators.note: half destroyed means the back half of the word is lost and only its first half kept

parts.note: shirts are worn on the upper body

explanation.surface: An Australian soldier's tops are ripped in a scuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: Diggers are Australian soldiers; imshi is their slang, from Arabic, for go away.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a slangy command telling someone to clear off, used by Australian troops.

clue.text: Rich club in charge

parts.note: an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: A wealthy golf club is the one running things.
explanation.walkthrough: Rich is used as in 'that's a bit rich', ironically absurd.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying a remark is rich means it is ironic, laughable given who says it.

clue.text: Switch like this from left to right

definitions.text: Switch like this from left to right

parts.words: Switch like this from left to right
parts.note: a two-way switch reads with its working position on the left and its dead one on the right

explanation.walkthrough: Read left to right, the two positions of a switch are named in turn; the setter had a car switch in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated word describes a switch with two settings, working and not working.

clue.text: The Listener's in confusion, having no tea

definitions.note: possessive phrase standing for an adjective: relating to the ear, what a listener uses

indicators.note: having no means the word for tea is removed

parts.note: chaotic means in confusion
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: The magazine's puzzle editors are in a muddle after running out of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener is a famous crossword series, a nice red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic is the anatomical adjective meaning of the ear, the organ a listener hears with.

clue.text: Lover to ace airman marshalled …

indicators.note: marshalled means arranged, as troops are lined up, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: to is taken as written and A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A sweetheart is assigned to a top pilot, as if by military order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marshalled' covers TO, the A for ace and AIRMAN together, shuffling all nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a woman who is someone's beloved or mistress.

clue.text: … support at Chamonix slope, with kit rejigged when temperature dropped

indicators.note: rejigged means rearranged, so the letters are put into a new order
dropped means the temperature letter is taken out of kit

explanation.surface: Equipment at a French ski resort is reorganised as the weather turns colder.
explanation.walkthrough: Chamonix is a ski resort in the French Alps, so the support is one used on the slopes.
explanation.definitionFit: A skier leans on a pole to push and balance, a support used in the Alps.

clue.text: Ripple of illegal activities gripping place

indicators.note: gripping means holding something tight, so the place letters go inside

parts.note: crime covers illegal activities collectively
PL is the map abbreviation for place

explanation.surface: A wave of criminality takes hold of a locality.
explanation.definitionFit: To crimple is to wrinkle or crinkle, giving a rippled surface.
